name: mean_reversion_speed_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The speed at which a stock reverts to its mean (VWAP) can be estimated by fitting an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process to the VWAP deviation series: dx = theta * (mu - x) * dt + sigma * dW. The theta parameter (mean-reversion speed) tells us how quickly deviations from VWAP are corrected. High theta (> 0.05 per bar): fast reversion, enter on large deviations and expect quick profit. Low theta (< 0.02 per bar): slow reversion, the deviation may persist, so avoid mean-reversion trades. By estimating theta in real-time on a 60-bar rolling window of VWAP deviations, we only trade mean-reversion when the statistical evidence supports it. The inefficiency exists because VWAP mean-reversion traders rarely quantify the reversion speed.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹75 Cr; stock must have stable VWAP (not dominated by single large trade)

indicators.name: VWAP_Dev
indicators.params: close - vwap (absolute deviation in price units)

indicators.name: OU_Theta
indicators.params: OLS regression: delta(VWAP_Dev) = theta * VWAP_Dev + intercept, window=60; theta = -slope

indicators.name: Expected_HL
indicators.params: log(2) / OU_Theta (expected half-life of reversion in bars)

conditions: Z_Score_VWAP < -2.0 (price significantly below VWAP in OU model terms)
long.confirmation: OU_Theta has been > 0.03 for at least 10 bars (stable mean-reverting regime)

short.confirmation: OU_Theta has been > 0.03 for at least 10 bars

exit.target: Z_Score_VWAP crosses zero (full reversion to VWAP)
exit.stop_loss: Z_Score_VWAP reaches -3.0 for longs / +3.0 for shorts (deviation worsens)
exit.trailing_stop: None — pure mean-reversion, target is VWAP
exit.signal_exit: OU_Theta drops below 0.02 (mean-reversion weakening — stop expecting reversion)

risk.position_sizing: Scale with OU_Theta: higher theta = more confidence = larger size. ₹75K if theta 0.05-0.08, ₹1L if 0.08-0.12, ₹1.25L if > 0.12

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22 (mean-reversion works best in calm markets)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 10:15 (need 60 bars for OU estimation) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Volume > SMA(volume, 20) — sufficient liquidity for VWAP to be meaningful
filters.trend_filter: abs(EMA(NIFTY_50, 30) - EMA(NIFTY_50, 60)) / EMA(NIFTY_50, 60) < 30 bps (index not in strong trend)
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day and RBI policy day
other_filters: OU regression R-squared > 0.10 (minimum fit quality for the OU model)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — OU process estimation for mean-reversion speed is a quantitative technique rarely applied to intraday VWAP trading; the statistical rigor provides a moat

weaknesses: OU process assumes constant theta and sigma within the 60-bar window — in reality, both parameters are time-varying (e.g., theta drops as VWAP deviation grows large), violating model assumptions
Z-score based on OU parameters inherits all estimation errors from theta and sigma — a 10% error in theta translates to large errors in Z-score and Expected_HL
The strategy only enters on Z_Score > 2.0, which combined with the high theta requirement, produces very few signals — may generate only 1-2 trades per day across entire universe
prior_art: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process for mean-reversion (Uhlenbeck & Ornstein 1930); applied to pairs trading in Bertram (2010); VWAP mean-reversion is common but formal OU estimation is rare
notes: Consider using maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) instead of OLS for OU parameters — MLE is more efficient for small samples. The theta threshold of 0.05 corresponds to a half-life of ~14 bars (14 minutes), which is reasonable for intraday mean-reversion.
